headline: Building an In-Law Apartment: How to Know When It Is Time to Call a Professional
articleBody:
Many homeowners start planning an in-law suite thinking it is just a weekend partition project, only to run into complex building requirements. Knowing when to bring in a licensed remodeling contractor saves you from code violations, safety hazards, and costly rework.

When Professional Guidance Helps
Look for these key indicators that your project requires professional construction expertise:
- Modifying structural walls: Cutting into load-bearing frames, shifting exterior door locations, or altering roof trusses demands engineered plans and proper temporary shoring.
- Expanding electrical and plumbing systems: Tying new showers, sinks, and dedicated kitchen circuits into existing service panels without causing overloads requires licensed trades.
- Complying with emergency egress and fire codes: Creating a safe living suite requires specific window opening dimensions, continuous ventilation, and fire-rated drywall barriers between shared dwellings.
- Handling local permits and inspections: Managing architectural filings, energy calculations, and mandatory municipal site inspections is best handled by experienced project managers.
- Addressing aging-in-place accessibility: Designing curbless walk-in showers, wider passageways, and secure backing for grab bars requires skilled trades who understand functional layouts.
